findings.problem: The same three-step proof of `earlierDummy ≠ freshVar-dummy` appears inline dozens of times in this one term. Each copy is `unfold <dummy>; with_reducible exact Nat.ne_of_lt (mem_lt_freshVar (nb084_support_mem_NNNN …) k)`. It pairs a support-membership lemma with a fresh-variable offset. Each copy repeats the full `show a ≠ b from by …` boilerplate, and the two parallel `A B R` and `x y A R` versions are written out separately for every `TAlphaVar.there`. This is hard to audit and bulks up the term. Note that `Nat.ne_of_lt` plus `mem_lt_freshVar` is itself short, so a helper is only worthwhile because of how many times it is repeated.
findings.proposed_change: Add one local helper next to this file's definitions, for example `theorem ne_freshVar_of_mem {s : Finset Var} {v : Var} (hv : v ∈ s) (k : Nat) : v ≠ freshVar s k := Nat.ne_of_lt (mem_lt_freshVar hv k)`. A second helper could return `TAlphaVar.there` directly from a membership proof, so a step becomes `ne_freshVar_of_mem (nb084_support_mem_0036 A B R) 1`. Each `show … from (by unfold …; with_reducible exact …)` block is then one application. The `unfold` is kept only where `freshVar` must be exposed, for example `(by unfold nb084AlphaDummy010; exact ne_freshVar_of_mem (nb084_support_mem_0036 A B R) 1)`. Both the `A B R` side and the `x y A R` side use the same lemma. Alternatively, fix the generator so it emits the helper call.
findings.benefit: This removes roughly 50 copies of the same proof from a 1,450-line term, so the remaining term shows which support lemma and offset justify each distinctness fact. A reader can then check the structure without scanning boilerplate. If the freshVar ordering argument changes, it needs one edit instead of dozens.

findings.problem: `nb084_focused_notmem_0010` to `0016` all prove `fresh dummy ∉ R.fv` in the same way. Each uses `change freshVar (R.fv ∪ … ) k ∉ R.fv`, then `freshVar_not_mem_of_subset k` with an inclusion proved by nested `Finset.mem_union_left`. There are only two shapes. In 0014–0016, the support is `R.fv ∪ A.fv ∪ B.fv`, with offsets 2, 1, 0. In 0010–0013, it is `R.fv ∪ A.fv ∪ cv a.fv ∪ cv b.fv`, with offsets 1, 0, 1, 0. The two-union inclusion and three-union inclusion are re-derived by hand seven times. The `change` statements also repeat the long support expression. The same pattern appears in other files such as `SingletonImageAlpha` and `CompositionAlpha`.
findings.proposed_change: Prove two lemmas once: `freshVar_not_mem_left3 (R A B : Class) (k : Nat) : freshVar (R.fv ∪ A.fv ∪ B.fv) k ∉ R.fv` and `freshVar_not_mem_left4 (R A C D : Class) (k : Nat) : freshVar (R.fv ∪ A.fv ∪ C.fv ∪ D.fv) k ∉ R.fv`. Prove each with `freshVar_not_mem_of_subset k (fun u hu => Finset.mem_union_left _ …)`. Then restate the uses as `nb084_focused_notmem_0014 A B R := freshVar_not_mem_left3 R A B 2`, `0015 := … 1`, `0016 := … 0`. `0010–0013` become `freshVar_not_mem_left4 R A (Class.cv _) (Class.cv _) k`, with `0011` and `0013` taking `(Class.cv x) (Class.cv y)`. The statements already unfold definitionally to the `change` goals, so only the `change` may need to stay.
findings.benefit: Seven near-identical proof blocks (about 70 lines) shrink to two lemmas plus one-line uses. This makes it clear that every dummy variable is fresh for R because of the same support-inclusion fact. The helpers can also be reused across the sibling alpha-support files that repeat this pattern, and adding another dummy needs one line.
